rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Full bold-span inventory taken this session (grep -noE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*' over lines 1-146) across all 10 chunks. Chunk 1 (lines 9,11,13): three 3-4 word noun-phrase handles, within cap — clear. Chunk 2 (line 17): one coined-sequence handle ('brainstorm → plan → work → simplify → review → compound'), a named artifact, one per slide — clear. Chunks 3/4/6/7: zero content bold besides the structural '**Read:**' label — clear. Chunk 5 (lines 58,60): two short (1-2 word) proper-noun handles naming the section's two distinct shipped artefacts (Feedback Loopable, Handoff) — terse named-term use, not sentence-leads — clear. Chunk 8 (lines 117-119,123-126,128) UNCHANGED by the diff-region edit at line 119 ('Seven design principles'→'Design principles' shortened the span but did not remove it): eight content-bold spans on one `##` slide — seven bulleted leads (A single orchestrator / Phase-organised skill catalogue. / Design principles / Front-loaded read-only analysis. / Mandatory gates fire positionally / Re-invocation as control flow. / CLAUDE.md as half the system.) plus one inline handle (scales cross-repo). None is a §34 task-sizing callout or a module-template LO bullet; not a reading-list/menu or lookup surface either. Per-slide COUNT is the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture the rule bans — still open, unactioned per orchestrator instruction from the prior sweep. NEW this session, pre-existing and previously unflagged: chunk 9 (lines 139,141,143), the 'Three filters' list, bolds the FULL question of every entry — 'What shape is your real work?' (6 words), 'How much orchestration do you want to author?' (8 words), 'What review bandwidth do you have?' (6 words) — all exceed the ≲5-word handle cap and none is a coined term/named law, they are ordinary authored questions. Considered and rejected as a covered menu-slide: the reading-list/menu waiver lifts the per-slide COUNT but explicitly does NOT lift the handle-length cap, and names the exact failure this is ('bold the mode word alone... leave the title plain. Bolding mode-plus-title is the pre-2026-07-09 monoculture wearing a list for cover') — here the entire question is bolded with the answer prose left plain, i.e. mode-plus-title with no plain title at all. Harm: on a slide with no size accept-note exempting it from projection, three consecutive full-sentence bolded leads flatten the bold signal into noise — a reader scanning for the slide's one handle finds three, none of which is a named concept, and the actual navigational cue (which practitioner to read) sits in plain unbolded prose at the end of each entry instead.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Chunk 8: keep bold on the 1-2 handles the slide most needs and flatten the rest to plain prose. Chunk 9: bold a short label per filter (e.g. **Real-work shape**, **Orchestration load**, **Review bandwidth**) and leave the question/answer prose plain, matching the mode-word convention used elsewhere.
